-122.34100,47.63260.name: Seattle Reproductive Medicine
-122.34100,47.63260.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Paul C. Lin, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-122.96564,49.16578.name: Virogin Biotech
-122.96564,49.16578.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, March 2026
-122.96564,49.16578.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, March 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-4.13343,5.31743.name: Institut Pasteur de Côte d'Ivoire
-4.13343,5.31743.state: Route de Dabou KM17 Adiopodoumé et Site Cocody CHU, Cote d'Ivoire
-4.13343,5.31743.company: Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research
-4.13343,5.31743.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, under construction. Run by Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Containment space: 140 SqM. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-71.08700,42.36300.name: Broad Institute — CRISPR patent estate
-71.08700,42.36300.desc: Holds the CRISPR patents that prevailed in the long US interference proceedings against Berkeley, covering use in plant and animal cells — which is to say, essentially every commercial application. The public money that funded the underlying work bought the public no rights in the result. Either side would have held the same estate had it won, and both sides built on publicly funded work.

-71.08700,42.36300.name: Genome Project-write
-71.08700,42.36300.state: Cambridge, Massachusetts — Center of Excellence for Engineering Biology
-71.08700,42.36300.desc: An international consortium working toward synthesising whole genomes, including eventually a human one. It was announced at a closed meeting in 2016, which caused an immediate argument about whether a project of that kind should be discussed privately at all, and its ethics programme dates from that reaction.

-78.87600,35.90200.name: Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies
-78.87600,35.90200.state: Morrisville, North Carolina — 101 J Morris Commons
-78.87600,35.90200.desc: A biologics contract manufacturer built by a photographic film company on the chemistry it already had — Fujifilm moved into biotechnology as film collapsed, using its expertise in collagen and thin-film coating. It now makes viral vectors and antibodies for other companies at some of the largest sites in Europe and the US, and is one of the reasons manufacturing capacity rather than approval is the constraint on cell and gene therapy.

-73.56600,45.50400.name: Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity
-73.56600,45.50400.desc: Runs the Cartagena Protocol and the Biosafety Clearing-House — the register this map draws its national decisions from. It is also where gene drives are argued over at treaty level, and where a moratorium on them has been proposed and rejected more than once. Almost every country is a party. The United States is not, and has never ratified the Convention itself.

10.18000,36.83000.name: Institut National de la Recherche Agronomique de Tunisie
10.18000,36.83000.desc: Works on durum wheat, olives and date palm for a warming, drying region. North Africa is where climate pressure on agriculture is arriving first and hardest, and the crops most affected are the ones with the least commercial breeding behind them.

2.27400,48.87000.name: OECD BioTrack — unique identifier database
2.27400,48.87000.desc: Where the international serial number on an engineered organism can be looked up. This map repeatedly says to write that identifier down; this is what it is for. Enter it and the database returns the organism, the applicant, the trait and which countries have ruled on it — the single string that ties a decision in one jurisdiction to the same organism in another. It only covers organisms carrying an inserted gene, because that is what the numbering system was built around, so an edited organism will not be found here and that absence is itself the answer.
